title: Pandemic preparedness
why: A new pandemic can cost millions of lives in a few years, and preparing is far cheaper than responding.
figure_text: excess deaths linked to COVID-19 in 2020 and 2021 (range 13.3 to 16.6 million), almost three times the deaths reported
status: WHO members adopted a Pandemic Agreement in May 2025, but it cannot be signed until its annex on sharing pathogens and benefits is agreed. Talks on the annex missed the May 2026 deadline and were extended to May 2027 at the latest.
status_source: WHO, World Health Assembly update (19 May 2026)

title: Clean water and sanitation
why: Unsafe water and sanitation spread disease, and collecting water takes hours a day in many places, mostly for women and girls.
figure_text: people without safely managed drinking water in 2024, about 1 in 4; 3.4 billion lack safely managed sanitation
source: WHO and UNICEF Joint Monitoring Programme (August 2025)
status: UN goal (SDG 6): safe water and sanitation for everyone by 2030. Safely managed drinking water reached 74% of people in 2024, up from 68% in 2015.

title: Plastic pollution
why: Plastic production doubled in 20 years, and most of the waste ends up in landfill, burned or in the environment.
figure_text: of plastic waste was recycled in 2019; 22% was dumped, burned in the open or leaked into the environment
status: No global treaty yet. Talks failed to agree at what were meant to be the final rounds in December 2024 and August 2025; a new chair was elected in February 2026 and talks continue.

title: Drug-resistant infections
why: When antibiotics stop working, common infections and routine surgery become dangerous again.
figure_text: deaths caused directly by antibiotic-resistant bacteria in 2021; the same study forecasts 1.91 million a year by 2050 without further action
status: UN members agreed in 2024 to cut deaths associated with drug-resistant bacteria by 10% by 2030, from 4.95 million in 2019.
status_source: UN General Assembly political declaration on AMR (2024)

title: Ocean protection
why: The ocean feeds billions of people and absorbs much of the heat and carbon we add, but most of it has no protection.
figure_text: of the ocean in protected or conserved areas (April 2026); only 1.3% is covered by areas whose management has been assessed
status: Global goal: 30% of land and sea protected by 2030 (Kunming-Montreal framework). The High Seas Treaty, which allows protected areas beyond national waters, came into force in January 2026.
